κἀγώ see: ἐγώ. ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς, of person(s) pron. I. (a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11]], [[mark 1 8|Mrk.1:8]], [[luke 3 16|Luk.3:16]], al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as [[matthew 10 16|Mat.10:16]], [[john 10 17|Jhn.10:17]]; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. [[1-kings 3 8|1Ki.3:8]]), [[acts 9 10|Act.9:10]]; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, [[john 1 23|Jhn.1:23]] (LXX), [[acts 7 32|Act.7:32]] (LXX). (b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, [[john 14 20|Jhn.14:20;]] μου τ. λόγους, [[matthew 7 24|Mat.7:24;]] ὀπίσω μου, [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11;]] ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, [[revelation 5 5|Rev.5:5;]] also with the prep. πρός, as [[mark 9 19|Mrk.9:19]], al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as [[luke 10 16|Luk.10:16]], [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23]], [[mark 14 7|Mrk.14:7]], al. (with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, [[matthew 2 6|Mat.2:6;]] μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, [[mark 9 24|Mrk.9:24.]] (d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, [[judges 11 12|Jdg.11:12]], al.), i.e. what have we in common: [[matthew 8 29|Mat.8:29]], [[mark 1 24|Mrk.1:24, 5:7]], [[luke 8 28|Luk.8:28]], [[john 2 4|Jhn.2:4]]; τί γάρ μοι, [[1-corinthians 5 2|1Co.5:2.]] (e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.). (f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: [[matthew 2 8|Mat.2:8]], [[luke 2 48|Luk.2:48]], [[john 6 56|Jhn.6:56]], [[romans 3 7|Rom.3:7]], [[1-corinthians 7 40|1Co.7:40]], al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, [[john 7 28|Jhn.7:28.]] (AS)

κατά (bef. a vowel κατ᾽, καθ᾽; on the frequently neglect of elision, see Tdf., Pr., 95; WH, App., 146a), prep. with genitive, accusative, down, downwards. I. C. genitive (WM, §47, k; Bl., §42, 2). 1. C. genitive of thing(s), in local sense; (a) down, down from: [[matthew 8 32|Mat.8:32]], [[mark 5 13|Mrk.5:13]], [[luke 8 33|Luk.8:33]], [[1-corinthians 11 4|1Co.11:4]]; (b) throughout (late usage; Bl, l.with): κ. ὅλης κ.τ.λ., [[luke 4 14|Luk.4:14 23:5]], [[acts 9 31|Act.9:31 10:37]]; (with) in a peculiar adjectival phrase: ἡ κ. βάθους, deep or extreme poverty, [[2-corinthians 8 2|2Co.8:2.]] 2. C. genitive of person(s), usually in hostile sense; (a) against (in cl. only after verbs of speaking, witnessing, etc.): opposite to ὑπέρ, [[mark 9 40|Mrk.9:40;]] μετά, [[matthew 12 30|Mat.12:30;]] after ἐπιθυμεῖν, [[galatians 5 17|Gal.5:17;]] λαλεῖν, [[acts 6 13|Act.6:13;]] διδάσκειν, [[acts 21 28|Act.21:28;]] ψεύδεσθαι, [[james 3 14|Jas.3:14;]] after verbs of accusing, etc., [[matthew 5 23|Mat.5:23]], [[luke 23 14|Luk.23:14]], [[romans 8 33|Rom.8:33]], al.; verbs of fighting, prevailing, etc., [[matthew 10 35|Mat.10:35]], [[acts 14 2|Act.14:2]], [[1-corinthians 4 6|1Co.4:6]], al.; (b) of swearing, by: όμνυμι κ. (BL, §34, 1), [[hebrews 6 13|He 6:13,16]], cf. [[matthew 26 63|Mat.26:63.]] II. C. accusative (WM, §49d; BL, §42, 2). 1. Of motion or direction; (a) through, throughout: [[luke 8 39|Luk.8:39 9:6 10:4]], [[acts 8 1|Act.8:1, 36]] al.; (b) to, towards, over against: [[luke 10 32|Luk.10:32]] (Field, Notes, 62), [[acts 2 1|Act.2:1]]o 16:7, [[galatians 2 11|Gal.2:11]], [[philippians 3 14|Php.3:14]], al.; (with) in adverbial phrases, at, in, by, of: κατ᾽ οἶκον, at home, [[acts 2 46|Act.2:46;]] κατ᾽ ἰδίαν (see: ἴδιος); καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν, [[acts 28 16|Act.28:16]], [[romans 14 22|Rom.14:22]], [[james 2 17|Jas.2:17]]; with pron. of person(s), [[acts 17 28|Act.17:28 18:15]], [[romans 1 15|Rom.1:15]], [[ephesians 1 15|Eph.1:15]], al. 2. Of time, at, during, about: [[acts 8 26|Act.8:26 12:1 19:23]], [[romans 9 9|Rom.9:9]] [[hebrews 1 10|Heb.1:10]], al. 3. Distributive; (a) of place: κ. τόποὐς, [[matthew 24 7|Mat.24:7]], al.; κ. πόλιν, [[luke 8 1|Luk.8:1]], 4 al.; κ. ἐκκλησίαν, [[acts 14 23|Act.14:23.]] (b) of time: κ. ἔτος, [[luke 2 41|Luk.2:41;]] ἑορτήν, [[matthew 27 15|Mat.27:15]], al.; (with) of numbers, etc.: καθ᾽ ἕνα πάντες, [[1-corinthians 14 31|1Co.14:31]] (on καθ᾽ εἷς, see: εἷς); κ. ἑκατόν, [[mark 6 40|Mrk.6:40;]] κ. μέρος, [[hebrews 9 5|Heb.9:5;]] κ. ὄνομα, [[john 10 3|Jhn.10:3.]] 4. Of fitness, reference, conformity, etc.; (a) in relation to, concerning: [[romans 1 3|Rom.1:3, 4 7:22 9:3, 5]], [[1-corinthians 12 6|1Co.12:6 10:18]], [[philippians 1 12|Php.1:12]]; κ. πάντα, [[acts 17 22|Act.17:22]], [[colossians 3 20|Col.3:20, 22]] [[hebrews 2 17|Heb.2:17 4:15]]; (b) according to, after, like: [[mark 7 5|Mrk.7:5]], [[luke 2 27|Luk.2:27, 29]] [[john 7 24|Jhn.7:24]] [[romans 8 4|Rom.8:4 14:15]], [[ephesians 2 2|Eph.2:2]], [[colossians 2 8|Col.2:8]], [[james 2 8|Jas.2:8]], al. III. In composition, κ. denotes, 1. down, down from (καταβαίνω), etc.), hence, metaphorically; (a) victory or rule over (καταδουλόω, -κυριεύω, etc.); (b) "perfective" action (M, Pr., 111ff.). 2. under (κατακαλύπτω), etc.). 3. in succession (καθεξῆς). 4. after, behind (καταλείπω). 5. Hostility, against (καταλαλέω). (AS)
